# `mutated-range-bound`

<!-- rule-docs:header (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
Tier: correctness · Profile: none · Default: warning · Fixes: none · Options: none

Reports an assignment to a local `var` used as a `for` range bound inside that
loop's body, which does not change how many times the loop runs.
<!-- /rule-docs:header -->

## Why it matters

A `for` range such as `0..count` is evaluated once, before the first
iteration. Updating `count` inside the body therefore does not shorten or
lengthen the loop: code that removes an element and decrements `count` to
skip it still visits every original index, often reading the element it just
moved or past the new end, and code that increments `count` after appending
never visits the new elements.

## When it fires

It reports the first in-place update (`count -= 1`, `count += 1`, any
compound assignment) of a local `var` used as the start or end of a range
input of a non-`inline` `for` loop, inside that loop's body. A plain
assignment such as `start = index` is not reported, because recording a
position for after the loop is the usual reason to write one, and neither is
an update directly followed by `break` or `return`, since the loop ends there.
Use a `while` loop with an explicit condition when the bound has to change.

<!-- rule-docs:footer (generated by `zig build rule-docs`) -->
## Example

```zig
fn dropZeros(values: []u32) usize {
    var count = values.len;
    for (0..count) |index| {
        if (values[index] == 0) {
            values[index] = values[count - 1];
            count -= 1;
        }
    }
    return count;
}
```
